claim: As of October 2026, Anthropic describes Claude Code as an agentic coding tool that reads your codebase, edits files, runs commands, and integrates with your development tools.

sources.title: Claude Code overview
sources.excerpt: Claude Code is an agentic coding tool that reads your codebase, edits files, runs commands, and integrates with your development tools.

claim: Claude Code runs in the terminal, in IDE extensions (VS Code, and JetBrains IDEs such as IntelliJ IDEA and PyCharm), in a desktop app and on the web; each surface uses the same engine, so a repository's CLAUDE.md files, settings and MCP servers work across all of them.

sources.title: Claude Code overview
sources.excerpt: Each surface connects to the same underlying Claude Code engine, so your repo's CLAUDE.md files, settings, and MCP servers work across all of them.

claim: For bugs and features, Claude Code plans the approach, writes code across multiple files and verifies it works; for a bug it traces the issue through the codebase to the root cause.

sources.title: Claude Code overview
sources.excerpt: Claude Code plans the approach, writes the code across multiple files, and verifies it works.

claim: Claude Code works directly with git (stages changes, writes commit messages, creates branches, opens pull requests) and can run in CI through GitHub Actions or GitLab CI/CD to automate code review and issue triage.

sources.title: Claude Code overview
sources.excerpt: In CI, you can automate code review and issue triage with GitHub Actions or GitLab CI/CD.

claim: Claude Code is scriptable: `claude -p` runs it non-interactively, so it can take piped logs, run in CI, or chain with other tools.

sources.title: Claude Code overview
sources.excerpt: Claude Code is composable and follows the Unix philosophy. Pipe logs into it, run it in CI, or chain it with other tools.

claim: Claude Code connects to external tools and data through the Model Context Protocol (MCP), an open standard (for example design docs in Google Drive, Jira tickets, or custom tooling).

sources.title: Claude Code overview
sources.excerpt: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open standard for connecting AI tools to external data sources.

claim: Teams customize Claude Code with CLAUDE.md (project instructions read at the start of every session), skills (shareable repeatable workflows such as /review-pr) and hooks (commands that run before or after Claude Code actions).

sources.title: Claude Code overview
sources.excerpt: CLAUDE.md is a markdown file you add to your project root that Claude Code reads at the start of every session.

claim: Claude Code can spawn multiple agents (subagents) that work on different parts of a task in parallel under a lead agent, and the Agent SDK lets teams build their own agents on Claude Code's tools and permissions.

sources.title: Claude Code overview
sources.excerpt: Spawn multiple Claude Code agents that work on different parts of a task simultaneously. A lead agent coordinates the work.

claim: The terminal CLI, VS Code and JetBrains surfaces support third-party providers (Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud, Microsoft Foundry), so they can run on cloud-provider credentials.

sources.title: Claude Code overview
sources.excerpt: The Terminal CLI, VS Code, and JetBrains also support third-party providers.

claim: A PreToolUse hook receives the tool name and input as JSON on stdin and can block the call by exiting with code 2 (its stderr is returned to Claude) or by returning a permissionDecision of deny.

sources.title: Hooks reference
sources.excerpt: Exit code 2 blocks the call... permissionDecision accepts allow, deny, ask, or defer.

claim: Project permission `allow` rules in a committed .claude/settings.json apply only after each developer trusts the folder, while `deny` and `ask` rules apply right away; OpenTelemetry exporter variables do not take effect from a repository file.

sources.title: Settings files and precedence
sources.excerpt: permissions.allow rules... apply only after each teammate trusts the folder... deny and ask rules apply right away.

claim: Claude Code installs on macOS, Linux and WSL with `curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash`, and native installations update automatically in the background.

sources.title: Claude Code overview
sources.excerpt: Native installations automatically update in the background to keep you on the latest version.

claim: As of October 2026, permissions.defaultMode sets the permission mode Claude Code sessions start in (default, labelled Manual; acceptEdits; plan; auto; dontAsk; bypassPermissions), and setting permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode or permissions.disableAutoMode to "disable" prevents bypass or auto mode from being used; both are most useful in managed settings, where they cannot be overridden.

sources.title: Configure permissions
sources.excerpt: To prevent bypassPermissions or auto mode from being used, set permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode or permissions.disableAutoMode to "disable" in any settings file.
